judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Plain and short, but 'Ogres or no Ogres, the [Place] stays open!' and the list-of-wares pattern ('Swords, axes, shields.') match the other new sets.

items.label: B
items.critique: Snow-in-the-door bit, hot cider, and a magic-shop pitch tied to the local threat ('the Undead don't care for fire') is a polished sales gag.

items.label: C
items.critique: 'Best ale on the river, and the only ale on the river!' and the 'Don't touch the jars' curmudgeon are crafted comic beats, too neat for Nox.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'Fish stew, fish pie, or fish. Heh, heh...' is a constructed joke; the wares list and threat-tied potion pitch repeat the packet's template.

items.label: E
items.critique: Plain shop introductions with a rival-inn comparison and the odd 'sir [Group]' address; functional and slightly stiff like Westwood's.

items.label: F
items.critique: 'aye mate?' oddity, 'Ya need some new weapons and armor? This is the place!', and an expository magic-shop line naming which guild it supplies: unpolished Westwood.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'pig-headed armored sheep marching up and down' is Westwood's cranky class-ribbing humour, and the drawn-out 'Ahhhhhhhh...' is typical.

items.label: H
items.critique: Brusque 'be quick about it', the class-aware 'Don't see many [Group] in my shop'; shares the Keep with E, which suggests a Westwood class variant.

items.label: I
items.critique: The undertaker-merchant offering 'funerary services' or goods and the pushy 'Let's get to know each other! Buy something!' are odd, specific Westwood touches.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'Pull up a stool and I'll pour you somethin' warm' is cosy stock inn phrasing; the class-aware arms line is close to Westwood, but the set is smooth.

tells: The new shopkeepers list their wares in threes ('Swords, axes, shields', 'Potions, scrolls, spell books') and tie the magic shop's pitch to the local monster; Westwood's rarely list stock.

New inn lines are built around a cosy or comic hook (snow at the door, a fish menu, best-and-only ale, a warm drink); Westwood's greetings are often flat, stiff, or oddly specific to the player's class and the plot.

Westwood's shopkeepers react to the player's class and situation (mocking armored 'sheep', noting rare visitors, spotting a key item), with eccentric word choices ('funerary services', 'aye mate'); the new ones are generic and clean.
Dialect spellings ('yer', 'fer', 'somethin'') used decoratively mark the new texts; Westwood's informality is in syntax more than spelling.
